name: Modern Life Is War
label: Deathwish
lede: Five friends from Marshalltown, Iowa, mailed out 100 copies of a 7-inch to book their own tour, put an 1896 photo of their Main Street on the cover of Witness, quit in 2008, and came back to write another record in a basement.

eras.title: Sixteen shows booked by mail
eras.text: The band forms in Marshalltown in 2002, presses a 7-inch and mails it out to book its own tour. A Martyr Records rep catches three shows and offers a full-length.

years.src: Punknews: Interview with Modern Life Is War · Punknews: Interview with Jeffrey Eaton · Wikipedia: Modern Life Is War
years.h: Childhood friends hand Eaton a band, and he hands them a mixtape
years.p: Friends from Marshalltown ask [[Jeffrey Eaton|1ba65c8b-4014-4d4a-bb09-dbff3e4c5d55]] to sing. He answers with a mixtape of The Trouble, Gorilla Biscuits, Minor Threat, Black Flag and In My Eyes, then they press a self-titled 7-inch.
years.xp:
The plan, Eaton told Punknews.org, was to save money, take second jobs if they had to, and put out their own 7-inch. They recorded it in Iowa at a studio that usually records church choirs and elementary school choruses.

He came to hardcore through a Rancid video on MTV in eighth grade, and Gorilla Biscuits' Start Today was the first hardcore record he loved. The rest of the band was guitarists John Eich and Matt Hoffman, bassist Chris Honeck and drummer Tyler Oleson. Wikipedia lists the 7-inch on Lifeline Records.

years.src: Punknews: Interview with Modern Life Is War
years.h: 100 copies of a 7-inch in the mail turn into 16 shows
years.p: The band offered promoters a free 15-minute opening slot and booked a tour with [[Champion|744cff3e-33b3-4f1c-b703-84aea4d811f7]], The Hope Conspiracy and Black Widows.
years.xp:
They drove a rusted-out 70s-style Dodge van, the kind every band from Marshalltown seems to have used. A Detroit show with Champion drew 40 kids. A night near Albany, New York, with Champion and The Promise drew over 100.

A Martyr Records rep came to three of the East Coast shows and offered them a full-length.

years.h: My Love. My Way. gets made in Brooklyn in March
years.p: The band records the debut LP at Atomic Recording Company: ten tracks, about 24 minutes.
years.xp: Wikipedia credits the release to Martyr Records, while its band page lists Lifeline Records for the album. [[Jacob Bannon|d5c2a3e1-a52a-4af6-8e3f-aa2c4dc69af7]] of [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]] co-directed the art with Christopher Cannon, and Deathwish Inc. later handled reissues, including a remaster with two bonus tracks from the 7-inch.

eras.title: Main Street on the sleeve
eras.text: Jacob Bannon's label puts out Witness, and two founding members leave right after.

years.cap: Jeffrey Eaton singing in Dublin, March 2005
years.src: Wikipedia: Witness · Wikipedia: Modern Life Is War
years.p: Recorded at Volume in Chicago and God City in Massachusetts, with [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]] mixing. It runs about 27 minutes.
years.xp: Alan Douches mastered it. Punknews.org ranked it fifth on its year-end list and wrote that if every album could be like it, "maybe music wouldn't suck as bad."

years.cap: Witness cover, with Main Street, Marshalltown, 1896
years.h: The cover is Marshalltown's Main Street in 1896
years.p: [[Jacob Bannon|d5c2a3e1-a52a-4af6-8e3f-aa2c4dc69af7]] designed the Witness sleeve around an 1896 photograph of the band's hometown.
years.xp: Bannon runs Deathwish Inc. and fronts [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]]. Sputnik Music gave the album five stars and called it "quite possibly the greatest hardcore album of our generation."

years.src: Wikipedia: Modern Life Is War · Punknews: Interview with Jeffrey Eaton
years.p: Matt Hoffman and Chris Honeck go in mid-2005. Sjarm 13 takes over guitar and Tim Churchman bass, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: Eaton told Punknews.org that Hoffman and Honeck left at different points, and that he felt the band's non-stop pace burned them out.

eras.title: A producer, a MySpace post
eras.text: A new line-up makes Midnight in America with J. Robbins, then ends the band six months later.

years.src: Wikipedia: Modern Life Is War · Punknews: Interview with Jeffrey Eaton
years.h: J. Robbins produces Midnight in America for Equal Vision
years.p: [[J. Robbins|3babd931-a940-43a8-b629-d7aed5b821d9]] produces the third album for Equal Vision Records, out August 21, 2007, with a cover of the folk song "Stagger Lee."
years.xp:
Alan Douches mastered it. Stylus Magazine gave it an A-. The line-up was Eaton, Eich, Sjarm 13, Churchman and Oleson.

Looking back, Eaton told Punknews.org that leaving Deathwish for Equal Vision was a mistake.

years.big: "I wish we took a break or six months off."
years.src: Wikipedia: Modern Life Is War · Punknews: Interview with Jeffrey Eaton
years.h: The band ends it with a MySpace post
years.p: Eaton on the February 19, 2008 breakup, six years and three albums in.
years.xp: The band had been touring non-stop since 2002. Eaton told Punknews.org the "can't stop, won't stop" mentality was "totally the reason why" it ended.

years.h: "Fuck the Sex Pistols" gets a video on the way out
years.p: The clip for the Midnight in America song lands in 2008, the year the band splits.

eras.title: A phone call from Arizona
eras.text: Chris Honeck asks, Jeffrey Eaton sets a condition, and the original five write a record in John Eich's basement.

years.big: "The only way I would consider it is if we all got together and wrote a new record."
years.src: Punknews: Interview with Jeffrey Eaton · Wikipedia: Modern Life Is War
years.p: Chris Honeck raises a reunion with [[Jeffrey Eaton|1ba65c8b-4014-4d4a-bb09-dbff3e4c5d55]] around March 2012. That was Eaton's answer.
years.xp:
Honeck had to play bass or it would not feel like Modern Life Is War, Eaton told Punknews.org. Between the breakup and the call Eaton had moved to California and was making his living DJing soul, funk, reggae and ska records.

Wikipedia says writing began in September 2012 in Eich's basement.

years.src: Punknews: Interview with Jeffrey Eaton · Wikipedia: Modern Life Is War
years.h: This Is Hardcore in Philadelphia is the first show back
years.p: Promoter Joe Hardcore invited them to play the festival, their first show in five years. Wikipedia says it and a record release show were all that was booked at first.
years.xp: Eaton told Punknews.org the comeback was "almost like nothing could quite live up to what I was hoping to happen." The plan was "mostly weekends, like two or three shows - maybe four, at max," since everyone had day jobs and limited vacation.

years.src: Wikipedia: Fever Hunting · Punknews: Interview with Jeffrey Eaton
years.h: Kurt Ballou engineers and mixes Fever Hunting at God City
years.p: First record in six years, out September 9, 2013 on Deathwish Inc.: 11 tracks, about 31 minutes.
years.xp:
Brad Boatright mastered it. Metacritic lists 81/100 and Pitchfork gave it 7.9. The band picked every act on the line-ups for its October release shows in Iowa, Chicago, Washington DC, New York and Boston.

Eaton told Punknews.org that leaving Deathwish earlier was a mistake, and that Bannon supplied artwork and handwritten lyrics for the return.

eras.title: Witness at ten, then the Tribulation records
eras.text: The band reissues Witness and puts out short releases when it feels like it.

years.cap: Live at Jewels Catch One, Los Angeles, December 12, 2015
years.h: Ten years on, Witness comes back remastered
years.p: Deathwish Inc. reissues the album on June 2, 2015 with new packaging and liner notes, then the band plays nine North American dates.

years.h: Tribulation Work Songs Vols. 1 and 2 arrive in 2018
years.p: Two EPs in one year, with an official Deathwish video for "Feels Like End Times."

years.h: Vol. 3 follows in 2021 with a video for "Survival"
years.p: The third Tribulation Work Songs volume comes out in 2021, with a clip for "Survival."

eras.title: Twelve years later
eras.text: Life on the Moon is the first full album since Fever Hunting.

years.h: Life on the Moon ends a 12-year wait
years.p: Out September 5, 2025 via Deathwish Inc. and Iodine Recordings. First single "Johnny Gone" came in June.
years.xp: Deathwish says the album was made over several years with longtime collaborator Brooks Strause and deals with loss and grief. Eaton described "Johnny Gone" as being about obsolescence and activism, touching on East Palestine, Ohio and Tehran, Iran.
